small_guidance:
- The instance-norm kernel is already fused and fast; the conv (nn.Conv2d 64→128, k=3, 128×128 input, batch 128) now dominates the 9.92ms runtime. Tuning the norm kernel further has minimal headroom — focus next iteration on the conv.
- If staying with current structure, try adding configs with BLOCK=2048 num_warps=4 and BLOCK=32768 num_warps=16 for the norm kernel, and consider a single-pass Welford variant to halve global memory traffic on the 16384-element rows.
- Ensure the norm kernel runs on channels_last layout if conv output is converted, so vectorized loads stay coalesced.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.Conv2d with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), tile sizes BLOCK_M=64/128 (OC), BLOCK_N=64/128 (spatial), BLOCK_K=32 over IC*kh*kw=576. Compute input gather offsets implicitly inside the kernel; this should dominate the speedup since conv is ~95% of runtime.
- Fuse the instance-norm + divide epilogue into a two-stage pipeline: conv writes to a workspace, then a single norm-div kernel reads/writes (current design). Alternatively, have the conv kernel accumulate per-(N,OC) sum and sum-of-squares using atomics into a small (N,OC) buffer while writing the conv output, so the second pass only needs to apply scale/shift — eliminating one full read of the 128×128×128×128 tensor.
- Use channels_last memory layout end-to-end so the GEMM-K (IC) dimension is contiguous and the norm reduction over H*W is contiguous per (N,C).
